_meta.feast: The Nativity according to the Flesh of our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ
_meta._note: Two-canon feast (1st by Cosmas of Maiuma in Tone 1, 2nd by John of Damascus in iambic verse Tone 1). OCA service text gives only the First Canon; the second canon is referenced but its text is not included. Magnificat replaced by ode-9 megalynaria (skipMagnificat: true). Great feast of the Lord — Having Beheld the Resurrection is suppressed.

troparion.text:
Thy Nativity, O Christ our God,
has shone to the world the light of wisdom!
For by it, those who worshipped the stars,
were taught by a star to adore Thee,
the Sun of Righteousness,
and to know Thee, the Orient from on high.//
O Lord, glory to Thee!
troparion.label: Troparion of the Nativity

kontakion.text:
Today the Virgin gives birth to the Transcendent One,
and the earth offers a cave to the Unapproachable One.
Angels with shepherds glorify Him;
The Wise Men journey with the star,//
since for our sake the eternal God was born as a little Child.
kontakion.label: Kontakion of the Nativity

sedalion.text:
Come, O faithful,
let us go to see where Christ was born!
We shall follow the Wise Men, kings from the East,
and be led by the guiding star
to the place where Angels sing unceasing praise.
Shepherds in the fields offer fitting hymns:
"Glory in the highest to Him Who today was born
of the Virgin Theotokos//
in a cave in Bethlehem of Judah!"
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 1)

sedalion.text:
Why dost thou marvel, O Mary?
Why art thou amazed at what has come to pass?
"I have given birth in time to a timeless Son;
I cannot explain how He was conceived in me.
I have known no man; how then shall I bear a child?
Who has ever seen a birth without seed?
When God so wills, as it is written:
'The order of nature is overcome.'"//
Christ is born of the Virgin in Bethlehem of Judah.
sedalion.label: Sessional Hymn (after Kathisma 2)

magnification.refrain:
We magnify Thee,
O Christ, the Giver of life:
Who for our sake now art born in the flesh of the Virgin Mary,
unwedded and most pure.
verses: Make a joyful noise unto the Lord, all the earth; sing the glory of His name; proclaim His glorious praise! (Ps. 65:1)
Our God is in heaven and on earth; He does whatever He pleases. (Ps. 113:11)

sessionalHymns.text:
How can a womb contain Him Whom nothing can contain?
How can He remain in His Father's bosom, yet rest in His Mother's arms?
It is His good pleasure to accomplish this.
Having no flesh, He purposely assumes it for our sake.
HE WHO IS becomes what He never was.
He shares our substance without forsaking His own nature.
Desiring to make us citizens of the world on high,//
Christ, the Only-begotten of the Father, is born on earth as a man.
sessionalHymns.label: Sessional Hymn after the Polyeleios

prokeimenon.refrain: "Out of the womb before the morning star have I begotten Thee." The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind.
prokeimenon.verse: The Lord said to my Lord: "Sit at My right hand, until I make Thine enemies Thy footstool."

gospel._note: The genealogy and birth of Jesus Christ.

postGospelSticheron.text:
Today all things are filled with joy,//
for Christ is born of the Virgin.
postGospelSticheron.label: Post-Gospel Sticheron (twice with Glory/Now/Both)

postGospelDoxasticon.text:
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace!
Today Bethlehem receives Him Who reigns forever with the Father.
Today Angels glorify the newborn Babe in hymns worthy of God:
"Glory to God in the highest,//
and on earth, peace, good will to men!"
postGospelDoxasticon.label: Doxasticon after Psalm 50

canon._author: First Canon by Cosmas of Maiuma; Second Canon by John of Damascus (text not in OCA source)
canon._canonNote: Two canons in Tone 1. OCA service text supplies only the first canon. The refrain 'Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!' precedes each troparion; the last troparion of each ode is preceded by 'Glory… now and ever…'.

ode1.irmos:
Christ is born, glorify Him!
Christ comes from heaven, go to meet Him!
Christ is on earth, be exalted!
Sing to the Lord, all the earth,
and praise Him in gladness, O people,
for He has been glorified!

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
troparia.text:
Man was made in the image of God,
but he sinned, and lost immortality.
He fell from the divine and better life,
enslaved completely by corruption.
Now the wise Creator fashions him again,
for He has been glorified.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
troparia.text:
The Creator shaped man with His own hands,
but when He saw us perishing eternally,
He bowed the heavens and came down to earth,
and clothed Himself completely in our nature,
truly incarnate from a pure and holy Virgin,
for He has been glorified.

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text:
Wisdom, and Word, and Power,
Christ our God is the Father's Son, His Radiance.
He was made man,
a mystery concealed from every spirit above or on the earth.
He has won us for Himself,
for He has been glorified.

ode3.irmos:
To the Son, begotten of the Father before all ages,
and incarnate of the Virgin
without seed in these latter days—
to Christ our God, let us cry out:
"Thou hast raised up our horn.
Holy art Thou, O Lord!"

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
troparia.text:
Adam was made from dust,
yet he shared God's life-giving breath.
He was deceived by woman and fell,
but from the dead, he saw Christ born of woman.
He shouted: "For my sake Thou hast become like me.
Holy art Thou, O Lord!"

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
troparia.text:
Thou hast assumed a body of lowly clay, O Christ.
By sharing our humble flesh,
Thou hast made our race partakers of divinity.
By becoming mortal man yet remaining God,
Thou hast raised us from death to life.
Holy art Thou, O Lord!

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text:
Make merry, O Bethlehem!
Thou art the king of Judah's princes.
Christ, the Shepherd of Israel,
Who rides on the shoulders of the Cherubim,
has come forth from thee for all to see.
He has raised us from death to life, and reigns over all.

sedalenAfterOde3.text:
Heaven brought the first-fruits of the Gentiles as a gift for Thee;
a star summoned the Wise Men to the babe in the manger.
They were amazed to see neither throne nor scepter, but only abject poverty.
What is more humble than a cave?
What is more lowly than swaddling clothes?
Yet the riches of Thy Divinity shone through all these.//
O Lord, glory to Thee!
sedalenAfterOde3.label: Hypakoe

sedalenAfterOde3.text:
Let the heavens rejoice and let the earth be glad!
The Lamb of God has been born on earth, granting redemption to the world.
The Word, Who rests in the bosom of the Father, has come forth without seed from the Virgin.
The Wise Men were struck with amazement, seeing Him born as an infant in Bethlehem.//
Let all creation glorify Him!
sedalenAfterOde3.label: Kathisma Hymn

ode4.irmos:
Stem and flower of the root of Jesse,
Thou hast blossomed from the Virgin, O Christ.
From the mountain overshadowed by the forest, Thou art come,
made flesh from her than knew no man.
O God, not formed from matter—
glory to Thy power, O Lord!

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
troparia.text:
Thou art the Expectation of the nations, O Christ,
foretold by Jacob in days of old.
Thou hast sprung from Judah's tribe,
to plunder the might of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria,
replacing error with faith acceptable to God.
Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
troparia.text:
Thou hast filled the stargazers with joy, O Lord.
They knew the hidden meaning of the Prophet Balaam's words.
Thou hast made the star of Jacob to rise.
As the first fruits of the Gentiles it led them unto Thee.
Thou didst openly receive their precious gifts.
Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text:
Thou didst descend into the Virgin's womb, O Christ,
like rain upon the fleece and raindrops watering the earth.
All earth's rulers fall down before Thee:
Ethiopia and the islands of Arabia,
the kings of Tarshish, of Sheba, and the Medes.
Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

ode5.irmos:
O God of Peace, Father of Mercies,
Thou hast sent Thine Angel of Great Counsel to grant us peace.
We are guided to the light of the knowledge of God,
and keeping watch by night,
we glorify Thee, O Lover of Man.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
troparia.text:
Thou wast registered as Caesar's subject, O Christ,
in obedience to his decree.
We were slaves of sin, and subject to the hateful enemy;
by Thy poverty Thou hast set us free.
Thou wast united to our nature in every way.
Though we were formed from dust,
by this communion we are made divine.

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text:
Behold, the Virgin, as foretold of old,
has conceived and given birth to God made man!
She remains a virgin still.
Through her we are reconciled to God.
Let us sinners faithfully sing her praise!
She is truly Theotokos!

ode6.irmos:
The sea monster cast forth Jonah as it had received him,
like a babe from the womb.
And when the Word came to dwell in the Virgin and was made flesh,
He came forth preserving her uncorrupt,
for as He Himself was not subject to decay,
He kept His mother free from harm.

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
troparia.text:
Christ our God has come in the flesh.
The Father begot Him from the womb before the Morning Star.
He rules the heavenly hosts,
yet now He lies in a manger of dumb beasts.
He Who looses the tangled knots of sin
now is wrapped in swaddling clothes.

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text:
A Son is born and given to the faithful,
a newborn Child of Adam's race,
yet He is Father and Ruler of the world to come.
He is called the Angel of Great Counsel.
He is the mighty God,
Who rules all creation by His might.

kontakion.text:
Today the Virgin gives birth to the Transcendent One,
and the earth offers a cave to the Unapproachable One.
Angels with shepherds glorify Him;
The Wise Men journey with the star,//
since for our sake the eternal God was born as a little Child.
kontakion.label: Kontakion of the Nativity

ikos.text:
Bethlehem has opened Eden. Come, let us see!
We have found joy in a secret place.
Come, let us seize Paradise hidden in the cave!
There the unwatered Root has appeared,
blossoming with forgiveness.
There is found the undug Well,
from which David longed to drink of old.
There the Virgin has borne a child,
quenching Adam's and David's thirst.
Let us hurry to this place,
(Oikos ending:)
where the eternal God was born as a little Child!

ode7.irmos:
The children, brought up together in godliness,
scorned the impious decree of the tyrant.
They were not afraid of the threat of fire,
but standing in the midst of the flames, they sang:
"Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
troparia.text:
The shepherds, abiding in the fields,
were terrified by a dazzling sight.
Around them shone the glory of the Lord.
An Angel shouted to them: "Sing praises!
The Messiah is born!"
Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
troparia.text:
After the Angel spoke,
the hosts of heaven suddenly cried out:
"Glory to God in the highest!
Peace on earth, good will to men!
Christ has shone forth."
Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text:
"What news is this?" asked the shepherds.
"Has God's Messiah truly come?
Let us go to Bethlehem!"
They saw Thee there, and worshipped Thee.
With Thy mother, they sang;
"Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

ode8.irmos:
The furnace, moist with dew,
was an image prefiguring a wonder beyond nature,
for it did not burn the children whom it had received,
nor did the Fire of Divinity consume the Virgin's womb when it entered it.
So let us raise the song:
"Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him throughout all ages!"

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
troparia.text:
The daughter of Babylon
drove David's children from Zion with sword and spear.
Now she sends her sons, the Wise Men,
bearing gifts, to worship in David's city, where God has come to dwell.
So let us raise the song:
"Let all creation bless the Lord and exalt Him throughout all ages!"

troparia.refrain: Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee!
troparia.text:
Grief had silenced the harps.
Zion's children would not sing in a foreign land.
But now Christ has shone forth in Bethlehem,
destroying the din of Babylon's idolatries.
So let us raise the song:
"Let all creation bless the Lord and exalt Him throughout all ages!"

troparia.refrain: Let us bless the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text:
Babylon plundered Zion,
and captured all her royal wealth.
But now, with a guiding star,
Christ lures her treasure-laden Wise Men back to Zion.
So let us raise the song:
"Let all creation bless the Lord and exalt Him throughout all ages!"

ode8._katavasiaCloser: We praise, bless, and worship the Lord, singing and exalting Him throughout all ages.

ode9.megalynarion:
Magnify, O my soul, the most pure Virgin Theotokos,
more honorable and more glorious than the heavenly hosts!

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, God, born in the flesh from the Virgin!
troparia.text:
The Wise Men saw a new, uncharted star,
following an unexpected course.
Its brightness surpassed every star in heaven.
It foretold the Messiah's birth: Christ, the King,
born on earth in Bethlehem, for our salvation.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the King born in the cave!
troparia.text: (Repeat: "The Wise Men saw a new…")

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, God, worshipped by the Wise Men!
troparia.text:
"Where is the newborn Infant-King?
We have seen His star," the Wise Men said.
"We have come to worship Him."
Godless Herod trembled with fury.
In his raging madness he plotted to kill Christ.

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the Lord Who revealed Himself to the Wise Men by a star!
troparia.text: (Repeat: "Where is the newborn Infant-King?…")

troparia.refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the pure Virgin who gave birth to Christ the King!
troparia.text:
Herod inquired when the star appeared
that had led the Wise Men to Bethlehem,
but after they worshipped Christ with gifts,
that same star led them back to their own land,
confounding their pursuer, that godless murderer of children.
Wise Men and shepherds came to worship Christ, born in the city of Bethlehem.

troparia.refrain: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
troparia.text: (Repeat: "Herod inquired when the star…")

ode9.katavasia:
Magnify, O my soul, the most pure Virgin Theotokos…
I behold a strange, most glorious mystery…
(or, the ninth heirmos of the second canon:)
Out of fear, we should choose to love silence,
for that is a safer course;
so difficult it is lovingly to compose intricately woven songs
to thee, O Virgin.
But grant us strength, O Mother,
equal to our natural calling.

exapostilarion.text:
Our Savior, the Dayspring from the East,
has visited us from on high,
and we, who were in darkness and shadow,
have found the Truth,
for the Lord is born of the Virgin.
exapostilarion.label: Exaposteilarion of the Nativity

stichera.verse: Praise Him for His mighty deeds; praise Him according to His exceeding greatness! (Ps. 150:2)
stichera.text:
Make glad, O you righteous!
Greatly rejoice, O heavens!
Dance for joy, O mountains, for Christ is born!
The Virgin has become like the cherubic throne.
She carries at her bosom God the Word, made flesh.
Shepherds glorify the newborn Child.
Wise Men offer the Master gifts.
Angels praise Him and sing://
"O Lord, past understanding, glory to Thee!"

stichera.verse: Praise Him with trumpet sound; praise Him with lute and harp! (Ps. 150:3)
stichera.text:
It was the good pleasure of the Father:
the Word is made flesh.
The Virgin gives birth to God made man.
A star announces the glad tidings.
Shepherds are amazed, and Wise Men worship,//
and creation is filled with mighty joy.

stichera.verse: Praise Him with timbrel and dance; praise Him with strings and pipe! (Ps. 150:4)
stichera.text:
Thou hast borne the Savior, O Virgin Theotokos.
Thou hast overthrown Eve's ancient curse.
Thou didst become the mother of the Son of God.
The Father is well-pleased in Him.
Thou dost carry at thy bosom God, the Word, made flesh.
We cannot fathom this mystery.
We can only believe, and give glory with thee://
O Lord, beyond all explanation, glory to Thee!

stichera.verse: Praise Him with sounding cymbals; praise Him with loud clashing cymbals! Let everything that breathes praise the Lord! (Ps. 150:5)
stichera.text:
Come, let us sing to the mother of the Savior,
who after childbearing remained a virgin:
"Hail, O spiritual city of God the King!
Christ came to dwell in thee.
He has accomplished salvation."
With Gabriel, let us sing her praise,
and with the shepherds, let us glorify her, crying out://
"O Theotokos, pray to Him Who took flesh from thee to save us!"

doxastikon.text:
When it was time for Thy coming on earth,
the first imperial taxation was held,
but Thou also didst take a census, O Lord,
recording the names of all men who believed in Thy birth.
Thou didst use the decree of Caesar for Thine own end:
to make manifest Thy timeless and eternal Kingdom.
Therefore we pay Thee our taxes, not with golden coins,
but with the riches of Orthodox theology,//
O God and Savior of our souls.
doxastikon.author: by Germanos

theotokion.text:
Today Christ is born of the Virgin in Bethlehem.
Today He Who knows no beginning, begins.
Today the Word is made flesh.
The powers of heaven greatly rejoice.
The earth makes merry with men.
The Wise Men offer gifts; the shepherds announce the wonder,
and without ceasing we cry aloud:
"Glory to God in the highest,//
peace on earth, good will to men!"
theotokion.author: by John the Monk

troparionAfterDoxology.text:
Thy Nativity, O Christ our God,
has shone to the world the light of wisdom!
For by it, those who worshipped the stars,
were taught by a star to adore Thee,
the Sun of Righteousness,
and to know Thee, the Orient from on high.//
O Lord, glory to Thee!
